title: ValidationPolicy::default() sets current_time_unix=0, silently failing all certs
description:
ValidationPolicy implements Default with current_time_unix = 0 (1970-01-01). The doc comment warns about this, and ValidationPolicy::new(now_unix) exists as the safe constructor. However, nothing prevents callers from writing ValidationPolicy::default() and getting a policy that rejects every certificate issued after 1970 with ValidityPeriod errors.

The struct is #[non_exhaustive], which means callers cannot use struct literal syntax. But they CAN write ValidationPolicy::default() and then modify individual fields without setting current_time_unix, because the field is pub. The failure mode is silent: the caller gets ValidityPeriod errors that look like the cert is expired/not-yet-valid, not an error that says 'you forgot to set the clock.'

What goes wrong if this stays as-is: Every caller who constructs via Default::default() and forgets to set current_time_unix gets mysterious ValidityPeriod failures. The failure is not self-diagnosing: the error says 'validity period check failed at chain index 0,' not 'current_time_unix is 0.'

This is documented but remains a footgun. The API shape forces every caller to write the same boilerplate ('set current_time_unix') — this is the defensive-code-forcing pattern from the review checklist. The workspace already has the correct constructor (ValidationPolicy::new(now_unix)), but Default provides a silently-wrong alternative.
